speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Meningococcemia (Neisseria meningitidis infection).

The clinical triad of high fever, a generalized nonpruritic rash, and a seizure in an infant, combined with the rash spreading from the trunk to extremities, is highly suggestive of invasive meningococcal disease. The lack of response to acetaminophen and the severity of the fever further support a bacterial etiology requiring immediate admission and IV antibiotics.
